description.narrative: Målet med förslagna insatsen är att stödja reformer inom finansiella sektorn för att skapa bättre förutsättningar för hållbar ekonomisk tillväxt. Insatsen kommer bidra till förbättra finansiell stabilitet, stödja utvecklingen av en mera hållbar och stabil banksektor och främja diversifiering inom finansiella sektorn i linje med europeiska standards. Detta kommer leda till en mera inkluderande finansiell sektor som gynnar både individer och små och mellanstora företag.

The goal of the contribution is to strengthen the financial sector so that it can function as a driver of economic growth. This will be achieved through implementing reforms aimed at enhancing financial stability, facilitating sustainable development of the banking sector, and promoting financial system diversification.

The objective of this technical assistance project is to strengthen the financial sector in Ukraine as a driver of sustainable and inclusive economic growth by implementing reforms aimed at enhancing financial stability and resilience, facilitate sustainable banking sector development and efficiency, and promote sustainable financial system diversification and inclusion. Ukrainian citizens and private enterprises are the ultimate beneficiaries of a more diversified and efficient financial sector, benefiting from more diverse and competitive financial services, ultimately leading to job creation and sustainable growth.

description.narrative:
Sida funded financial sector programs implemented by the World Bank have been instrumental in helping authorities achieve key reforms to stabilize and deepen the financial sector in Ukraine. This project was a logical continuation of the previous Swedish funded technical assistance. In the wake of the full-scale invasion the financial sector support program adapted to the changing needs and fluid situation on the ground. In line with this, the World Bank has under this program provided assistance to authorities in launching a war risk insurance mechanism in Ukraine (the relevant law developed with assistance of the project lodged with Parliament in December 2024), improved the regulatory framework for capital markets, housing finance mechanisms (given that damages and losses in housing sector are the largest according to WBs RDNA assessment), as well as promoting a cashless economy and higher take-up of digital financial services to deepen financial intermediation and inclusion.
The World Bank considers Ukraine's EU candidate status and the process of EU accession negotiations to be key drivers of financial sector reform processes. World Bank Sida funded technical assistance programs is also stated by the World Bank to have played a critical role in advancing reforms in Ukraine's non-bank financial sector. These reforms have enhanced regulatory capacity, market stability, and financial inclusion, contributing to building a transparent, resilient, and investor friendly non-bank financial sector in Ukraine, aligned with EU directives and standards. Non-bank financial sector became better supervised and regulated leading to its cleanup from nonviable institutions.
With technical assistance from the Sida funded project and supported by Development Policy Loan operation of the World Bank Ukrainian authorities imposed and enforced strict rules of related party lending and conduct related party diagnostics, implemented EU-compliant credit risk assessment, banks capital structure, prudential norms and banks liquidity measures, leading to much stronger, resilient and transparent banking sector.
The financial safety nets were strengthened which facilitated a cleanup of the banking sector and allowing to conduct bank resolutions since 2017 without involving state capital. The Deposit Guarantee Fund became financially and operationally resilient. SOB corporate governance was strengthened with the introduction of majority independent Supervisory Board. This enabled State Owned Bank's restructuring which will facilitate a future possible privatisation.
